villa-general-belgrano.name: Villa General Belgrano
villa-general-belgrano.summary: A mountain village in Córdoba province, Argentina, named after independence hero Manuel Belgrano and known today for its Oktoberfest celebrations reflecting local German heritage.

s-o-paulo-museum-of-art.name: MASP
s-o-paulo-museum-of-art.summary: An art museum in São Paulo founded in 1947 by Assis Chateaubriand and Pietro Maria Bardi, housed in a landmark 1968 building by architect Lina Bo Bardi, known for its European art collection.

lina-bo-bardi.name: Lina Bo Bardi
lina-bo-bardi.summary: Italian-born Brazilian modernist architect (1914–1992) who promoted the social potential of architecture and design, drawing on Brazilian vernacular style despite facing prejudice as a foreign woman.

oscar-niemeyer.name: Oscar Niemeyer
oscar-niemeyer.summary: Brazilian architect (1907 to 2012) and key figure of modern architecture, known for designing Brasília's civic buildings and for pioneering expressive, curving reinforced-concrete forms.

assis-chateaubriand.name: Assis Chateaubriand
assis-chateaubriand.summary: Brazilian lawyer, journalist, politician and diplomat (1892–1968) who founded Brazil's Diários Associados media conglomerate and served as ambassador to the UK.

pietro-maria-bardi.name: Pietro Maria Bardi
pietro-maria-bardi.summary: Italian writer and curator (1900–1999) who co-founded and long directed the São Paulo Museum of Art after moving to Brazil in 1946.

aracy-amaral.name: Aracy Amaral
aracy-amaral.summary: Brazilian art historian and curator (1930-2026), professor at the University of São Paulo and museum director, known for her scholarship on Brazilian modernism, especially Tarsila do Amaral.

tarsila-do-amaral.name: Tarsila do Amaral
tarsila-do-amaral.summary: Brazilian painter, draftswoman and translator (1886–1973), regarded as a leading Latin American modernist who helped define a nationalistic Brazilian modern art style.

museum-of-contemporary-art-university-of.name: Museum of Contemporary Art, University of São Paulo
museum-of-contemporary-art-university-of.summary: Contemporary art museum on the University of São Paulo campus and in Ibirapuera Park, one of the largest art museums in Brazil.
museum-of-contemporary-art-university-of.source_title: Museum of Contemporary Art, University of São Paulo

wesley-duke-lee.name: Wesley Duke Lee
wesley-duke-lee.summary: Brazilian painter, born and died in São Paulo (1931 to 2010).

cildo-meireles.name: Cildo Meireles
cildo-meireles.summary: A Brazilian conceptual artist, installation artist and sculptor born in 1948, known for large installations that express resistance to political oppression in Brazil.

h-lio-oiticica.name: Hélio Oiticica
h-lio-oiticica.summary: Brazilian visual artist and theorist (1937–1980) known for his participation in the Neo-Concrete Movement, his innovative use of color and 'environmental art' like the Parangolés and Tropicália.

mira-schendel.name: Mira Schendel
mira-schendel.summary: Brazilian artist (1919–1988) known for drawings on rice paper, also active as painter, poet and sculptor, whose work explored language and poetry.

brazilian-expeditionary-force.name: Brazilian Expeditionary Force
brazilian-expeditionary-force.summary: The Brazilian military division, nicknamed the 'Smoking Snakes,' that fought with Allied forces in the Mediterranean theatre of World War II, taking over 20,000 Axis prisoners.

primeiro-comando-da-capital.name: Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC)
primeiro-comando-da-capital.summary: A Brazilian criminal organization based in São Paulo, considered Latin America's biggest drug gang, running over half of Brazil's cocaine exports to Europe as of 2023.

comando-vermelho.name: Comando Vermelho
comando-vermelho.summary: A Brazilian criminal organization formed in 1979 among convicts and political prisoners, which later turned to drug trafficking and today controls parts of Rio de Janeiro.

brazilian-battleship-minas-geraes.name: Minas Geraes
brazilian-battleship-minas-geraes.summary: A Brazilian dreadnought battleship, laid down in 1907, whose 1910 mutiny (the Revolt of the Lash) over racism and abuse spread across the navy.

brazilian-battleship-s-o-paulo.name: São Paulo (battleship)
brazilian-battleship-s-o-paulo.summary: A Brazilian dreadnought battleship, sister ship to Minas Geraes, built by Vickers and commissioned in 1910, involved in the Revolt of the Lash mutiny.

natal-rio-grande-do-norte.name: Natal
natal-rio-grande-do-norte.summary: Capital of Brazil's Rio Grande do Norte state, founded in 1599; its strategic Atlantic-coast location made it a key U.S. airbase site during World War II.

operation-torch.name: Operation Torch
operation-torch.summary: Allied invasion of French North Africa from 8 to 16 November 1942, landing forces at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers under General Eisenhower to open a front against Axis forces.

fam-lia-do-norte.name: Família do Norte
fam-lia-do-norte.summary: A criminal faction controlling parts of northern Brazil and neighboring countries, considered the third-largest such faction in Brazil and the largest in Amazonas state.

boa-vista-roraima.name: Boa Vista
boa-vista-roraima.summary: The capital of Brazil's Roraima state, on the Branco River near the Venezuelan and Guyanese borders, and the only Brazilian state capital located entirely north of the equator.

german-submarine-u-43.name: U-43
german-submarine-u-43.summary: A German submarine launched in 1914 that served in World War I until it surrendered on 20 November 1918.

freetown.name: Freetown
freetown.summary: The capital and largest city of Sierra Leone, a major Atlantic port founded in 1792 by freed African Americans, Afro-Caribbeans and Liberated Africans as a settlement for freed slaves.

fernando-de-noronha.name: Fernando de Noronha
fernando-de-noronha.summary: An archipelago of 21 islands in the Atlantic off Brazil's coast, part of Pernambuco state, with about 3,100 residents and a national marine park since 1988.

united-states-office-of-war-information.name: Office of War Information
united-states-office-of-war-information.summary: A U.S. government agency active from 1942 to 1945 that used media to connect the battlefront and civilians and ran propaganda campaigns abroad during World War II.
united-states-office-of-war-information.source_title: United States Office of War Information

office-of-the-coordinator-of-inter-ameri.name: Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs
office-of-the-coordinator-of-inter-ameri.summary: A US agency established in 1940 under Nelson Rockefeller to promote cooperation with Latin America and counter Axis propaganda there during World War II.
office-of-the-coordinator-of-inter-ameri.source_title: Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs

guardi-es-do-estado.name: Guardiões do Estado
guardi-es-do-estado.summary: A Brazilian criminal faction operating in Ceará state, known for violence including bus burnings and the Cajazeiras massacre.

cear.name: Ceará
cear.summary: A state on Brazil's northeastern Atlantic coast, with the capital Fortaleza, known for its long coastline and as one of the country's main tourist destinations.

modern-art-week.name: Week of Modern Art
modern-art-week.summary: An arts festival in São Paulo, Brazil, held 10 to 17 February 1922, that marked the start of Brazilian Modernism through exhibitions, lectures, concerts and poetry readings at the Municipal Theater.

cam-es-prize.name: Camões Prize
cam-es-prize.summary: The most prestigious literary prize for Portuguese-language writing, established in 1989 and funded by Brazil and Portugal, awarded annually with a €100,000 prize.

cordel-literature.name: Cordel literature
cordel-literature.summary: Cheaply printed Brazilian booklets of folk novels, poems, and songs, sold in street markets and named for the strings from which they are hung on display.

elicura-chihuailaf.name: Elicura Chihuailaf
elicura-chihuailaf.summary: Mapuche Chilean poet born in 1952, who writes in both Mapudungun and Spanish and records his people's oral tradition. In 2020 he became the first Mapuche writer to win Chile's National Prize for Literature.

mapudungun.name: Mapudungun
mapudungun.summary: The language of the Mapuche people, spoken in south-central Chile and west-central Argentina, with no official national status in either country.

oswald-de-andrade.name: Oswald de Andrade
oswald-de-andrade.summary: Brazilian poet, novelist and critic (1890–1954) who co-founded Brazilian modernism and took part in the 1922 Modern Art Week in São Paulo.

manifesto-antrop-fago.name: Manifesto Antropófago
manifesto-antrop-fago.summary: A 1928 essay by Brazilian poet Oswald de Andrade, inspired by a painting by Tarsila do Amaral, arguing for Brazilian modernist culture built by 'devouring' foreign influences.

m-rio-de-andrade.name: Mário de Andrade
m-rio-de-andrade.summary: A Brazilian poet, novelist and critic (1893–1945) whose 1922 poetry collection helped launch modern Brazilian literature, and who led São Paulo's Modern Art Week that year.

manuel-bandeira.name: Manuel Bandeira
manuel-bandeira.summary: A Brazilian poet, literary critic and translator (1886-1968) who wrote over 20 books of poetry and prose.

cassiano-ricardo.name: Cassiano Ricardo
cassiano-ricardo.summary: Brazilian journalist, literary critic, and poet (1895–1974) associated with the nationalist currents of Brazilian modernism, whose later work turned to concrete poetry.

machado-de-assis.name: Machado de Assis
machado-de-assis.summary: Pioneering Brazilian novelist, poet and playwright, 1839 to 1908, widely regarded as Brazil's greatest writer, who founded the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1897.

cruz-e-sousa.name: Cruz e Sousa
cruz-e-sousa.summary: Brazilian poet and journalist (1861–1898), descended from African slaves, known as one of Brazil's first Symbolist poets and nicknamed the 'Black Dante'.

lima-barreto.name: Lima Barreto
lima-barreto.summary: Brazilian novelist and journalist (1881–1922), a major figure in Brazilian Pre-Modernism best known for his satirical novel Triste Fim de Policarpo Quaresma.

gilberto-freyre.name: Gilberto Freyre
gilberto-freyre.summary: Brazilian sociologist, anthropologist, historian and writer (1900 to 1987) best known for his treatise The Masters and the Slaves.

recife.name: Recife
recife.summary: A major port city on Brazil's northeastern coast, founded in 1537; it was known as Mauritsstad when it served as capital of the 17th-century Dutch colony of New Holland.

frevo.name: Frevo
frevo.summary: A Brazilian Carnival dance and music style from Recife, named for the Portuguese word for 'to boil', recognized by UNESCO in 2012.

paubrasilia.name: Brazilwood
paubrasilia.summary: A Brazilian timber tree prized for its dense red heartwood, used in stringed-instrument bows and as a source of red dye; the source of Brazil's name.

esmeralda-ribeiro.name: Esmeralda Ribeiro
esmeralda-ribeiro.summary: Brazilian journalist and writer born 1958, a member of the Afro-Brazilian literary group Quilombhoje since 1982 and editorial coordinator of its Cadernos Negros anthology series.

jo-o-guimar-es-rosa.name: João Guimarães Rosa
jo-o-guimar-es-rosa.summary: Brazilian novelist, short-story writer and diplomat (1908–1967) whose only novel, Grande Sertão: Veredas, blended archaic and colloquial language and is often likened to James Joyce's Ulysses.

the-devil-to-pay-in-the-backlands.name: Gran Sertón: Veredas
the-devil-to-pay-in-the-backlands.summary: 1956 novel by Brazilian writer João Guimarães Rosa, celebrated for its reinvention of the Portuguese language and now regarded as one of the greatest works of Brazilian literature.
the-devil-to-pay-in-the-backlands.source_title: The Devil to Pay in the Backlands

l-cio-cardoso.name: Lúcio Cardoso
l-cio-cardoso.summary: Brazilian novelist, playwright and poet, 1912 to 1968.

brazilian-academy-of-sciences.name: Brazilian Academy of Sciences
brazilian-academy-of-sciences.summary: Brazil's national academy of sciences, headquartered in Rio de Janeiro and founded on May 3, 1916.

national-council-for-scientific-and-tech.name: CNPq
national-council-for-scientific-and-tech.summary: A Brazilian government agency that promotes scientific and technological research and trains researchers, under the country's Ministry of Science and Technology.
national-council-for-scientific-and-tech.source_title: National Council for Scientific and Technological Development

finep.name: Finep
finep.summary: A Brazilian federal agency under the Ministry of Science and Technology that funds scientific research and technology projects.

national-institute-for-space-research.name: INPE
national-institute-for-space-research.summary: Brazil's civilian space and atmospheric research institute, based in São José dos Campos, working alongside the Air Force's aerospace technology command.

national-institute-of-amazonian-research.name: INPA
national-institute-of-amazonian-research.summary: A Brazilian research institution founded in 1952 in Manaus, dedicated to studying the Amazon's tropical forests, ecology, zoology and botany.

jos-sarney.name: José Sarney
jos-sarney.summary: José Sarney: Brazilian politician, lawyer and writer who served as the 31st president of Brazil from 1985 to 1990, becoming president after running mate (and presidential candidate) Tancredo Neves died before taking office.

petrobras.name: Petrobras
petrobras.summary: Brazilian majority state-owned oil corporation headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, ranked among the world's largest energy companies.

venceslau-br-s.name: Venceslau Brás
venceslau-br-s.summary: A Brazilian politician (1868–1966) who served as the 9th President of Brazil from 1914 to 1918, after earlier serving as governor of Minas Gerais and as Vice President.

italian-campaign-world-war-ii.name: Italian Campaign
italian-campaign-world-war-ii.summary: Allied and Axis military operations in and around Italy from 1943 to 1945, beginning with the invasion of Sicily and ending with the Axis surrender in Italy in May 1945.

declaration-by-united-nations.name: Declaration by United Nations
declaration-by-united-nations.summary: A 1942 treaty in which Allied nations of World War II formally pledged joint action against the Axis powers; it later became the basis for founding the United Nations in 1945.

get-lio-vargas.name: Getúlio Vargas
get-lio-vargas.summary: Brazilian president (1882–1954) who ruled from 1930–1945 and 1951–1954, seen by historians as the most influential Brazilian politician of the 20th century.

neo-scholasticism.name: Neo-scholasticism
neo-scholasticism.summary: A revival and development of medieval Scholasticism in Catholic theology, also called neo-scholastic Thomism for its debt to Thomas Aquinas, beginning in the late 19th century.

scholasticism.name: Scholasticism
scholasticism.summary: Medieval European method of philosophical and theological study, dominant from about 1100 to 1700, using rigorous logical debate to reconcile Aristotle's philosophy with Christian theology.

thomism.name: Thomism
thomism.summary: The philosophical and theological school built on the work of Thomas Aquinas, whose writings remain central to Catholic philosophy and theology.

brazilian-institute-of-philosophy.name: Brazilian Institute of Philosophy
brazilian-institute-of-philosophy.summary: A private cultural institution in São Paulo founded in 1949 by jurist and philosopher Miguel Reale, contributing to legal theory, metaphysics and philosophy of science.

miguel-reale.name: Miguel Reale
miguel-reale.summary: A Brazilian jurist and philosopher (1910–2006) known for the three-dimensional theory of law, who founded the Brazilian Institute of Philosophy in 1949.

julio-cabrera-philosopher.name: Julio Cabrera
julio-cabrera-philosopher.summary: Argentine philosopher living in Brazil, a retired professor at the University of Brasília, known for his work on 'negative ethics' and on cinema and philosophy.

university-of-bras-lia.name: University of Brasília
university-of-bras-lia.summary: A federal university founded in 1962 in Brazil's capital, especially known for its economics, international affairs and political science programs.

duns-scotus.name: Duns Scotus
duns-scotus.summary: Scottish Franciscan friar and philosopher-theologian (c. 1265–1308), ranked among the most important medieval thinkers, known for ideas such as 'haecceity' and an argument for God's existence.

auguste-comte.name: Auguste Comte
auguste-comte.summary: French philosopher (1798–1857) who coined the term sociology and founded the doctrine of positivism, influencing thinkers such as John Stuart Mill.

immanuel-kant.name: Immanuel Kant
immanuel-kant.summary: German Enlightenment philosopher (1724–1804) whose work on knowledge, ethics and metaphysics, especially the Critique of Pure Reason, made him among the most influential thinkers in Western philosophy.

henri-bergson.name: Henri Bergson
henri-bergson.summary: French philosopher (1859 to 1941) who argued intuition mattered more than rationalism for understanding reality, and won the 1927 Nobel Prize in Literature.

summa-theologica.name: Summa Theologica
summa-theologica.summary: Thomas Aquinas's best-known work, written in his mature years, summarizing Catholic theology by reconciling Aristotelian philosophy with Christian belief; one of the most influential works of Western thought.

summa-contra-gentiles.name: Summa contra Gentiles
summa-contra-gentiles.summary: A four-book treatise Thomas Aquinas wrote between 1259 and 1265 that uses reason rather than scripture to defend Christian belief to non-believers.

estado-novo-brazil.name: Estado Novo
estado-novo-brazil.summary: Getúlio Vargas's dictatorial regime in Brazil from 1937 to 1945, marked by nationalism, centralized power, anti-communism and authoritarianism.

capoeira.name: Capoeira
capoeira.summary: An Afro-Brazilian martial art blending dance, acrobatics, music and spirituality, rooted in the Angolan Bantu tradition and once criminalized before Brazil legalized it in 1937.

manuel-dos-reis-machado.name: Mestre Bimba
manuel-dos-reis-machado.summary: Brazilian capoeira master (1899/1900–1974) who founded the capoeira regional style and helped legitimize capoeira in Brazilian society.

prudent-polis.name: Prudentópolis
prudent-polis.summary: A Brazilian municipality in the state of Paraná, home to the center of the Ukrainian community in Brazil, with a population of about 49,000 and surrounded by 100 waterfalls.

paran-state.name: Paraná
paran-state.summary: One of Brazil's 26 states, in the south of the country, bordered by Argentina and Paraguay, with its capital at Curitiba.

pierre-verger.name: Pierre Verger
pierre-verger.summary: French photographer and self-taught ethnographer (1902–1996) who became a Yoruba priest and devoted his life to studying the African diaspora and its religions.

bahia.name: Bahia
bahia.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil holding about 7% of the country's population, with its capital Salvador on the Bay of All Saints.

candombl.name: Candomblé
candombl.summary: An African diasporic religion that developed in 19th-century Brazil, blending West and Central African traditions, especially Yoruba, Bantu and Gbe beliefs, with Roman Catholicism.

umbanda.name: Umbanda
umbanda.summary: Religion that emerged in Brazil in the 1920s, blending Spiritism, Afro-Brazilian traditions and Roman Catholicism; its followers, Umbandistas, seek guidance from spirits through mediums.

liberation-theology.name: Liberation theology
liberation-theology.summary: A Christian theological approach that began among Latin American Catholic theologians in the 1960s, stressing liberation of the oppressed through social and economic analysis.

seicho-no-ie.name: Seicho-No-Ie
seicho-no-ie.summary: A Japanese new religion emphasizing gratitude for nature, family, ancestors and one universal God, the world's largest New Thought group with over 1.6 million followers by 2010.

babalawo.name: Babalawo
babalawo.summary: A Yoruba spiritual title meaning 'father of secrets', denoting a high priest of the Ifá divination system who helps preserve Yoruba language, proverbs and customs.

brazil_southern_cone-modern-art-009: University of São Paulo's Museum of Contemporary Art
brazil_southern_cone-modern-war-010: Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs
